title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Base the Escalation Acts On, by What the Term Delivered
content:
## Service coordinator ruling

The base the escalation acts on, in pricing a further term of a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record, follows what the term just ending actually delivered. A visit closed as no-access consumes none of the visits credited and is not counted among the visits completed. The reading is the visits completed on the agreement against the visits the term credited.

| Reading | The base the escalation acts on |
|---|---|
| the visits completed stand above the visits the term credited | the annual price in force together with the tier's price for one additional visit for each visit beyond them |
| the visits completed stand below the visits the term credited | the annual price in force less the tier's price for one additional visit for each visit short of them |
| the visits completed match the visits the term credited | the annual price in force |

### Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

An agreement whose annual price in force is 5 400.00 USD, whose term credited 8 visits, at a tier whose price for one additional visit is 340.00 USD:

- 10 visits completed: 2 beyond the credited visits, so the base is 5 400.00 USD together with 340.00 USD multiplied by 2, that is 6 080.00 USD.
- 6 visits completed: 2 short of the credited visits, so the base is 5 400.00 USD less 680.00 USD, that is 4 720.00 USD.
- 8 visits completed: the base is 5 400.00 USD.
- 9 visits completed of which 1 was closed as no-access: the no-access call is not counted among the visits completed, so 8 stand against 8 credited and the base is 5 400.00 USD.
